title: Report On History Of Police Force Is Traced By Speake

page_data.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 27, 1937
History Of Police Force Is
Traced By Speaker
Deputy Commissioner Young Gives Interesting
Outline Of Development Of Settlement's Law
Guardians; Early Days And Difficulties Recalled

Another of the interesting talks arranged by the British Residents' Association was given yesterday evening at the Assembly Hall of the Cathedral School for Boys, when Mr. S. C. Young, Deputy Commissioner of the S.M.P., outlined the development of the Police Force of the Settlement and the manner in which its growth was identified with the history of the city.

In addressing the large gathering present Mr. Young said, in part:—
It can be said with a considerable amount of truth that the history of the Shanghai Municipal Police is the history of the International Settlement.

It is of interest to remember that although the British Settlement first came into being in 1843, it was not until 1854 that authority was obtained for the establishment of a Police Force. The first Land Regulations of 1845 expressly forbade such an establishment and only permitted the employment of watchmen approved by the Chinese Officials of that time. However unsatisfactory this may have been, it should be borne in mind that there were few foreigners in the Settlement in its early years and the Chinese residents could be numbered in hundreds.

In 1853 came the Small Swords members of the Triad Secret Society who captured the Chinese City, and the Chinese population was increased to approximately 20,000 by the influx of refugees. The admission of Chinese to the Settlement was contrary to the agreement then in existence which laid down that no new Chinese residents could be admitted and the original Chinese residents were expressly forbidden to rent houses to each other or to build for the purpose of renting to other Chinese.

Police Force Created
It was the situation created by the influx of refugees that necessitated the revision of the Land Regulations and the creation of a Police Force. Land Regulation 10 of the revised regulations of 1854 permitted the organization "of a watch or police force" and thus what you now know as the Shanghai Municipal Police came into existence.

The Settlement was at that time entirely British and the Consul had complete control. The American Settlement had been in existence for some time in the area now known as Hongkew. In 1863 the British and American Settlements were united to form the International Settlement. It has been said that one of the main causes of the amalgamation was that Hongkew had become the home of the undesirable and criminal elements owing to the efficiency of the Police in the British Settlement.

Strength Of Force
The first police force consisted of eight men under a Superintendent, but this grew to approximately 30 during the Taiping Rebellion when the Chinese population grew to about 400,000 as the result of the attack on the Chinese City and the ravaging of the surrounding countryside by the Taipings. In 1860, when the Taiping Rebellion collapsed in 1864, many of the Chinese left for their former homes, and the population declined to about 20,000.

Those interested will find that this was the time of the first land crisis when land values which had been greatly inflated tumbled to depths comparatively far below anything lately experienced. The economic crisis which resulted led to the appointment of the first economy commission, and this led to the reduction of the Force which then stood at 164 and which up to that time had consisted entirely of foreigners.

In 1865 Chinese Constables were recruited for the first time, and we find in that year a total of 61 foreigners and 42 Chinese. In 1884 Sikhs were enlisted principally for the policing of Bubbling Well and Jessfield Roads. From that time the Force has gradually increased and in 1916, 30 Japanese were appointed. To-day the strength of all branches of the Force is 452 foreigners, 272 Japanese, 555 Sikhs and 3,452 Chinese.

Difficulties Faced
Shanghai, as many of you know, presents difficulties from a police point of view which exist in no other place, and the successful and efficient administration of a police force in this area is an important part of the Council's service to this community.

The higher control is vested in a commissioner who has under him five Deputy Commissioners of the regular police and one Volunteer Deputy Commissioner who is responsible for the control of that useful volunteer body popularly known as the 'Specials.'

Four Divisions
For administrative and executive purposes the Settlement is divided into four police divisions lettered A, B, C and D. A and B divisions are situated south of the Soochow Creek and C and D to the north of that line. Each division has its headquarters in a police station in the division, and each headquarters has a Divisional Officer who may be either an Assistant Commissioner or a Superintendent who is in complete charge of the division and a Divisional Detective Officer, usually a Superintendent, who is responsible for the investigation of all crimes committed in his division.

In turn, each division consists of three or four police districts. Each police district is a self-contained unit consisting of uniform and detective staffs and is so organized that everything outside of extraordinary situation can be handled by it without assistance from any other station. The Divisions come under the control of the Deputy Commissioner in charge known as D.C. (Divisions) and thus you see the line from the Constable on the beat, through the Inspector in charge of the District, and Divisional Headquarters, to the Deputy Commissioner who is in close touch with the Commissioner.

All crime reports similarly percolate from the Stations to the Deputy Commissioner responsible to the Commissioner for crime investigation.

Headquarters Staff
The more important administrative work in connection with the personnel is carried out at Police Headquarters. There is a Japanese Deputy Commissioner who assists the Commissioner where his branch is concerned and a Chinese Deputy Commissioner who looks after the needs of the large Chinese Staff in a similar way.

An important section of the Force at Headquarters is the Special Branch which consists of a staff of detectives under a Deputy Commissioner. It is their work to deal with political matters of all kinds, unions, labour strikes and anything that may tend to disturb the peace and good order of the Settlement. This branch keeps in close touch with Division, etc., and can usually give an indication of possible disturbances to come in order that preparation can be made to meet them.

Mr. Young then proceeded to outline the various departments under the Municipal Police located at Headquarters, and their respective duties. These included the Traffic Department, Armed and Training Reserve, Stores, Armoury, Transport Section, Fingerprint, Arms Identification, Photographic Studio, Printing Section, Modus Operandi Section, Narcotic Section, Crime Branch Headquarters, Telephone and Wireless Sections and Boarding House Section.

The Specials
Continuing he said:—
The Specials deserve more time than I have at my disposal this evening. Since their formation during the war period they have assisted the regular police whenever required and with an enthusiasm that is beyond praise. They also do a fair amount of patrolling and as a body of volunteers, founded on the British model, they merit the support of the British community here.

I have, so far, kept away from the subject of finance. You all know that the Police Force requires a considerable proportion of the Municipal Estimates. The peculiar condition under which this force has to labour necessitates a greater proportion of strength to population than you find elsewhere, but the comparison between its cost and that of forces elsewhere is of some interest. Such a comparison shows that the proportionate cost, on a population basis, is less than half of what it is in London and less than a third of the cost in Los Angeles.

Surrounding Areas
The position of the Settlement from a geographical and an administrative point of view makes the work of the force extraordinarily difficult. The nine square miles comprising this area is, as you know, surrounded by areas under entirely separate jurisdictions. However close the co-operation between the police forces outside and ours, any action we wish to take outside involves formalities which not only militate against the successful conclusion of the project, but entail a use of manpower out of all proportion to that required when operating in our own territory. And when I tell you that of 10,000 persons arrested for the more serious crimes in 1936 only 3,176 were residents of the Settlement you will realize...

《字林西报》，1937年2月27日，星期六

演讲者追溯警队历史
副总监杨氏简述租界法律守护者的演变历程；回顾早期岁月与艰难处境

英国侨民协会安排的系列有趣讲座之一，于昨晚在男座堂学校（Cathedral School for Boys）的礼堂举行。上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）副总监 S. C. Young 先生概述了租界警队的发展历程，以及其成长如何与这座城市的历史紧密相连。

杨先生在向在场的大量听众致辞时部分说道：——

可以说，在很大程度上，上海公共租界警务处的历史就是国际租界的历史。

值得一提的是，虽然英租界最早成立于1843年，但直到1854年才获得建立警队的授权。1845年的首部《土地章程》明确禁止设立此类机构，仅允许雇用经当时中国官员批准的更夫。尽管这种情况可能令人不满，但应铭记的是，租界早期外籍居民寥寥无几，而中国居民仅数以百计。

1853年，三合会秘密社团的小刀会成员攻占了中国县城，随着难民的涌入，中国人口增加至约2万人。允许华人进入租界违反了当时存在的协议，该协议规定不得接纳新的中国居民，并明确禁止原有中国居民相互出租房屋或为出租给其他华人而建造房屋。

**警队的创建**

正是难民涌入所造成的局面，使得修订《土地章程》和创建警队成为必要。1854年修订后的章程第10条允许组织“更夫或警队”，因此，如今众所周知的上海公共租界警务处由此诞生。

当时的租界完全由英国人主导，领事拥有完全的控制权。美租界已在如今称为虹口（Hongkew）的地区存在了一段时间。1863年，英租界和美租界合并组成国际租界。据说，合并的主要原因之一是，由于英租界警队的高效运作，虹口已成为不良分子和犯罪元素的聚集地。

**警队兵力**

最初的警队由一名督察长统领下的八名警员组成，但在太平天国运动期间，随着对中国县城的攻击及太平军对周边乡村的蹂躏，中国人口增长至约40万，警队规模也随之扩大至约30人。1860年，当太平天国运动于1864年瓦解时，许多华人返回故乡，人口下降至约2万人。

感兴趣的人会发现，这正是第一次土地危机时期，此前被大幅炒高的地价暴跌至远低于近期任何经历的低谷。由此引发的经济危机导致任命了第一个节约委员会，进而导致警队裁员。当时警队人数为164人，且在此之前完全由外籍人士组成。

1865年，首次招募华捕，当年共有外籍警员61名，华捕42名。1884年，主要为了维持静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）和极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的治安，招募了锡克教警员。从那时起，警队规模逐渐扩大，1916年任命了30名日籍警员。如今，警队各分支的总兵力为：外籍警员452名，日籍警员272名，锡克警员555名，华捕3,452名。

**面临的困难**

正如诸位所知，上海在警务方面存在着其他地方所没有的困难，在该地区成功且高效地管理警队是工部局服务于本社区的重要组成部分。

最高控制权归属于一名总监，其下辖五名正规警队副总监，以及一名志愿副总监，后者负责控制那支被通俗称为“特别巡捕”（Specials）的有用志愿队伍。

**四个分区**

出于行政和执行目的，租界被划分为四个警区，分别标记为 A、B、C 和 D 区。A 区和 B 区位于苏州河以南，C 区和 D 区位于该线以北。每个分区在其辖区内的一个警察局设有总部，每个总部设有一名分区官，可以是助理总监或督察长，全面负责该分区的事务；另设有一名分区侦缉官，通常由督察长担任，负责调查其分区内发生的所有犯罪案件。

此外，每个分区由三到四个警段组成。每个警段是一个自给自足的单元，由制服警员和侦缉人员组成，其组织方式使得除特殊情况外，所有事务均可在不借助其他警局协助的情况下处理。各分区受分管副总监（简称 D.C. (Divisions)）的控制，因此你可以看到从巡街警员，到负责警段的巡官，再到分区总部，直至与总监保持密切联系的副总监这一指挥链条。

所有犯罪报告同样从各警局层层上报至负责犯罪调查并向总监汇报的副总监。

**总部职员**

与人事相关的重要行政工作在警务处总部进行。设有一名日籍副总监，在其所属分支事务上协助总监；另设有一名华籍副总监，以类似方式照顾庞大的华籍职员队伍的需求。

总部警队的一个重要部门是政治部（Special Branch），由一名副总监领导下的侦缉人员组成。他们的工作是处理各类政治事务、工会、劳工罢工以及任何可能扰乱租界和平与良好秩序的事项。该部门与各分区等保持密切联系，通常能预示可能发生的骚乱，以便做好准备加以应对。

随后，杨先生概述了位于总部的公共租界警务处下属各个部门及其各自职责。这些部门包括交通科、武装与训练后备队、仓库、军械库、运输科、指纹科、武器识别科、摄影室、印刷科、作案手段科（Modus Operandi Section）、禁毒科、犯罪科总部、电话与无线电台科以及寄宿公寓科。

**特别巡捕**

他继续说道：——

特别巡捕值得我花费比今晚更多的时间来介绍。自他们在战争期间组建以来，每当需要时，他们都以无可赞誉的热情协助正规警队。他们还承担相当数量的巡逻任务，作为一支基于英国模式建立的志愿队伍，他们值得在此地的英国侨民社区的支持。

到目前为止，我一直避开财政话题。众所周知，警队占据了市政预算相当大的比例。这支警队必须在特殊条件下运作，这使得其警力与人口的比例高于其他地方，但其成本与其他地方警队的比较颇有意思。这种比较显示，按人口比例计算的成本不到伦敦的一半，也不到洛杉矶的三分之一。

**周边地区**

从地理和行政角度来看，租界的地位使得警队的工作异常艰难。众所周知，构成该区域的九平方英里土地被处于完全独立管辖权下的地区所包围。无论外部警队与我们之间的合作多么紧密，我们要在辖区外采取的任何行动都涉及繁琐的手续，这不仅阻碍项目的成功完成，而且所需的人力与其在我们自己领土内行动时所需相比完全不成比例。当我告诉你，1936年因较严重罪行被捕的10,000人中，只有3,176人是租界居民时，你就会意识到……

LONDON ORGANIZATION : It was appreciated at the outset that the most effective way of fulfilling the responsibilities with which the Association was entrusted would be the creation of an effective organization in London. On the invitation of the Committee, Messrs. O. M. Green, E. F. Mackay, H. G. Simms and P. C. Young, C.B.E., agreed to serve as a London Committee. On the recommendation of this Committee, a Publicity Agent and a Political Agent were appointed in London. The cost of the London organization—exclusive of cables, stationery and similar charges—is £1,000 per annum. This organization has kept in close touch with Members of both Houses, with British commercial organizations, and with the leading British newspapers, and has done valuable work in educating the British public regarding the problems of the British communities in China.

FINANCES : The membership fee of the Association was originally fixed at $1.00 per annum, but as soon as it was decided to establish the London organization, it became apparent that far more substantial funds would be necessary, and an appeal was therefore addressed to members for special contributions. The result was most satisfactory, the amount received during the year being Tls. 30,755.32, which included a grant of Tls. 6,021.52 from the Shanghai Information Service. Of this amount Tls. 13,360.16 is now on fixed deposit. The expenses of the Association are set forth in detail in the statement of accounts.

CO-OPERATION WITH OTHER ORGANIZATIONS : The Committee has throughout the year maintained cordial relations with the Committees of the British Chamber of Commerce and the China Association (Shanghai Branch), to whom it is indebted for much valuable assistance in securing information required for the London Committee, and also with the Outports. On several occasions resolutions and memoranda endorsed by all three bodies have been communicated to His Majesty's Government.

LETTERS AND CABLES : The number of local and foreign letters despatched during the year was 615, which included 54 addressed to the London Committee. Letters and circulars to the Outports numbered 658 ; eight circulars were issued to Members ; and sixty-nine circulars were sent to the members of the Committee.

Nineteen cables were sent to and sixteen received from London.

STAFF : The Association has been permitted to use a portion of the office accommodation of the British Chamber of Commerce at a nominal rental, and also to avail itself of the services of the Chamber's Secretariat.

财务：本会的会费原定为每年1.00美元，但一旦决定建立伦敦机构，显然需要更雄厚的资金，因此向会员发出特别捐款的呼吁。结果令人非常满意，本年度收到的款项为规元30,755.32两，其中包括来自上海信息服务处的拨款规元6,021.52两。其中规元13,360.16两现已存入定期存款。本会的支出详情列于账目报表中。

与其他组织的合作：委员会全年与英国商会委员会及中国协会（上海分会）委员会保持着融洽的关系，本会在获取伦敦委员会所需信息方面得益于它们的大量宝贵协助，同时也与外埠保持着联系。经这三个机构共同认可的决议和备忘录曾多次呈递给英王陛下政府。

Mr. H. G. W. WOODHEAD.—It has devolved upon me
to propose a resolution on the subject of extraterritoriality.
It is unnecessary to emphasise to an audience composed
entirely of Britons in Shanghai the vital importance of
this question. A false step now would adversely affect
the welfare and the interests of British residents in China,
not only of the present but of future generations. Extra-
territoriality affects almost every phase of our lives in this
country, domestic, business and professional. A single
false step now may produce irreparable disaster, and it is
because I believe that such a false step is contemplated
by H. M. Government that this meeting is going to be
asked to express its views on the subject. It is common
knowledge that negotiations for the abolition of extra-
territoriality have been taking place between the British
Minister and the Chinese Foreign Office at Nanking, and
it has been reported in the Press that a draft treaty has
actually been drawn up, whilst according to some authori-
ties it has actually been initialled. This has given rise
to much apprehension amongst the British residents of
Hankow and Tientsin lest their interests are to be sacri-
ficed on the altar of expediency. We have been told
that the negotiations and the draft treaty that has been
prepared as a result thereof are in accordance with the
avowed policy of the British Foreign Office. I propose
to show you that, on the contrary, they represent a com-
plete reversal of the policy announced in 1929, and that
they come perilously near to actual betrayal of our in-
terests in China. You may recall that, in April, 1929,
the Chinese Government, claiming that the assimilation
of western legal conceptions and the incorporation of
Western legal principles in Chinese jurisprudence were
making rapid progress, demanded that extraterritoriality
be abandoned as promptly as possible. What was the
British Government's reply ? This is a point I want to
emphasise as indicating the state of affairs, and so I will
read the most important passage in the British Govern-
ment's reply of August of the same year. It was :—

“His Majesty's Government would, however, observe
that the promulgation of codes embodying Western

W. 伍德黑德先生：由我来提出一项关于治外法权问题的决议。向在座完全由在上海的英国人组成的听众强调这一问题的重要性是多余的。此刻的任何错误步骤都将对在华英国侨民的福祉和利益产生不利影响，这不仅关乎当下，也关乎子孙后代。治外法权影响着我们在这个国家生活的几乎各个方面，包括家庭、商业和职业生活。此刻哪怕迈出错误的一步，都可能造成无法挽回的灾难；正是因为我相信英国陛下政府正考虑迈出这样错误的一步，所以才请本次会议就此问题表达观点。众所周知，英国驻华公使与南京中国外交部之间一直在进行废除治外法权的谈判，据媒体报道，条约草案实际上已经拟定，而据某些权威人士称，该草案甚至已经草签。这引起了汉口和天津英国侨民的极大担忧，唯恐他们的利益会被牺牲在权宜之计的祭坛上。我们被告知，这些谈判以及由此产生的条约草案符合英国外交部公开宣称的政策。我打算向各位证明，事实恰恰相反，它们代表了对1929年宣布政策的彻底逆转，并且已危险地接近于实际上背叛我们在华利益。大家可能还记得，1929年4月，中国政府声称西方法律观念的同化以及西方法律原则纳入中国法理学的工作进展迅速，因此要求尽快废除治外法权。英国政府的答复是什么？这一点我想强调一下，以表明事态状况，因此我将宣读同年8月英国政府答复中最重要的段落。内容如下：

“然而，英国陛下政府指出，颁布体现西方

page_data.en:
4 SHANGHAI BRITISH RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION

legal principles represents only one portion of the task
to be accomplished before it would be safe to abandon
in their entirety the special arrangements which have
hitherto regulated the residence of foreigners in China.
In order that those reforms should become a living reality,
it appears to H.M. Government to be necessary that
Western legal principles should be understood and be
found acceptable by the people at large, no less than by
their rulers, and that the Courts which administer these
laws should be free from interference and dictation at
the hands, not only of military chiefs, but of groups and
associations who either set up arbitrary and illegal tri-
bunals of their own, or attempt to use legal Courts for the
furtherance of political objects rather than for the ad-
ministration of equal justice between Chinese and Chinese,
and between Chinese and foreigners. Not until these
conditions are fulfilled in a far greater measure than
appears to be the case to-day will it be practicable for
British merchants to trade and own property throughout
the territories of China with the same equality of freedom
and safety as those privileges are accorded to Chinese
merchants in Great Britain. Any agreement purporting
to accord such privileges to British merchants would, for
some time to come, be a mere paper agreement to which it
would be impossible to give effect in practice. Any
attempt prematurely to accord such privileges would not
only be of no benefit to British merchants, but might
involve the Government and people of China in political
and economic difficulties."

That was what the British Government thought in
August, 1929. It will be seen that certain very vital
principles were laid down as essential preliminaries to the
abandonment of the special safeguards under which we
live and trade and do our ordinary business in China
to-day. I will mention only two. The first was the
elimination of military interference with the functions of
the judiciary. Recently we have had a flagrant example
of the failure of the Government to eliminate this inter-
ference. I refer to the Thorburn case. The truth of
this tragedy—the whole truth—is still unknown, although
page_data.zh:
4 上海英国侨民协会

法律原则的法典，仅是在安全地完全放弃迄今为止规范外国人在华居住的特殊安排之前所需完成任务的一部分。为了使这些改革成为活生生的现实，英国陛下政府认为，有必要让广大民众而不仅是其统治者理解并接受西方法律原则，并且执行这些法律的法院应免受干涉和指令，这种干涉和指令不仅来自军事首领，还来自那些要么设立任意的非法法庭，要么试图利用法律法院来推进政治目标而非在中国人之间以及中外之间施行平等正义的团体和协会。只有在这些条件得到比目前看来更大程度的满足时，英国商人在中国全境贸易和拥有财产才能享有与英国给予中国商人的同等自由和安全特权。任何旨在授予英国商人此类特权的协议，在相当长的一段时间内，将仅仅是一纸空文，在实践中无法生效。任何过早授予此类特权的尝试，不仅对英国商人毫无益处，反而可能使中国政府和人民陷入政治和经济困境。”

这就是英国政府在1929年8月的看法。可以看出，当时确立了一些非常关键的原则，作为放弃我们今天在中国生活、贸易和开展日常业务所依赖的特殊保障的必要前提。我只提及其中两点。第一点是消除军事对司法职能的干涉。最近我们有一个明显的例子，表明政府未能消除这种干涉。我指的是索恩伯恩（Thorburn）案。这场悲剧的真相——全部真相——仍然未知，尽管

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI BRITISH RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION 5

the British Government is apparently willing to accept
the Chinese Government's belated statement as to what
occurred. We should like to know what happened to
John Thorburn between June 2 and June 8, when he was
alleged to have been shot by Col. Huang, and whether
he was really shot ; because an eye-witness, who gave a
statement to the North-China Daily News stated that he
had seen him, bound and bleeding, and crying out in
Chinese :—" Save my life," on June 10, being led through
Soochow under a military escort, two days after he is
supposed to have been shot. That military interference
has not ceased can be amply proved—another single
reference to the Nakamura case in Manchuria will suffice.

Secondly, the British Government insisted on the
suppression of groups and associations who set up arbi-
trary tribunals of their own. If you think that the sup-
pression of these groups has been effected, I need only
refer you to the present practices of the boycotting com-
mittees in Shanghai. Most of you are aware that they
actually had the audacity to establish a prison and a so-
called court for the control of Chinese offenders against
their self-constituted regulations, within the reserved area
of the Settlement itself. I do not think I am disclosing
any confidences when I say that the British Chamber of
Commerce has received frequent complaints of the con-
fiscation of British goods under the mistaken impression
that they were of Japanese origin.

It is no exaggeration to assert that the very
abuses which the British Government regarded in
1929 as constituting insuperable obstacles to the
abolition of extraterritoriality flourish and continue
to flourish to-day, and would still flourish even
if paper safeguards were incorporated in any treaty
purporting to effect their suppression, and yet what do
we see the British Government doing ! In May this
year, the Chinese Government announced that extra-
territoriality would be abolished on January 1, 1932, in
spite of the fact that we enjoy these rights under treaties
which are still valid. And, instead of insisting on the
sanctity of these treaties, the British Government under-
page_data.zh:
上海英国侨民协会 5

英国政府显然愿意接受中国政府就所发生事件作出的迟来声明。我们想知道约翰·索恩伯恩（John Thorburn）在6月2日至6月8日期间发生了什么，据称他在此期间被黄上校枪击，以及他是否真的被枪击；因为一位向《字林西报》提供陈述的目击者称，他在6月10日看到索恩伯恩被捆绑着、流着血，并用中文高喊：“救救我的命”，当时他正由军队押解穿过苏州，而这距离据称他被枪击的时间已过去两天。军事干涉并未停止，这一点可以得到充分证明——只需再举一个满洲的中村（Nakamura）案的例子就足够了。

其次，英国政府坚持镇压那些设立任意法庭的团体和协会。如果你认为这些团体的镇压已经实现，我只需提请你们注意上海抵制委员会目前的行径。你们大多数人都知道，他们竟敢在租界保留地范围内设立监狱和所谓法庭，以管制违反其自定规章的中国违规者。我说英国商会频繁收到投诉，称英国货物因被误认为是日本原产而遭到没收，我认为这并没有泄露任何机密。

毫不夸张地说，英国政府在1929年视为废除治外法权不可逾越障碍的那些弊端正盛行并持续盛行至今，即使在任何旨在抑制这些弊端的条约中加入纸面上的保障措施，它们仍将继续盛行。然而，我们看到英国政府在做什么！今年5月，中国政府宣布将于1932年1月1日废除治外法权，尽管我们依据仍然有效的条约享有这些权利。而且，英国政府没有坚持这些条约的神圣性，而是

page_data.en:
6 SHANGHAI BRITISH RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION

took negotiations with Nanking which, to the best of our
belief, have resulted in one surrender after another of the
vital rights and interests of the foreign communities. In
1931, as in 1929, the premature abandonment of safe-
guards such as are now enjoyed would have been not only
of no benefit, but would have involved the Government
and people of China in difficulties.

One of the unfortunate consequences of the
policy pursued by our Government, as was pointed
out by a very distinguished Scot who recently left
Tientsin, was that we have been driven "as our
only defence against the too precipitate action of
our own Government to lay emphasis on the worst
features of the Chinese character, and, when we do not
wish to be too open, in our condemnation, to blazon
China's shame even in the Press of this country." We
all know that the Chinese have good points, but they
have not yet been manifested in the administration of
justice. Even Chinese propagandists do not now fall
back on the superiority of Chinese law. In a letter only
a few days ago, we were invited to become "fellow
victims" in the struggle against the forces of oppression
and injustice. "Fellow victims" mark you. If we find
it difficult to continue that struggle now, how much more
difficult will it be when the safeguards which enable us to
continue that fight have been abolished? I suggest, as
others have done, that any resolution adopted to-night
should be unanimous. It would be fatal to have any
influential body of local opinion disassociating themselves
from this new body. We must aim to give reasonable
views and to secure as far as possible the sympathy of
those at Home and in other parts of China, so as to secure
a reconsideration of the extraterritoriality issue. The
Committee have drafted a resolution which may not
appear strong enough to some of you, but it does cover
the main points at issue. The British Government's
view appears to be that the situation is such that the con-
clusion of any new treaty prior to January 1 next is better
than having no treaty at all. How can it be seriously
argued that a treaty must be concluded to supplant a valid
page_data.zh:
6 上海英国侨民协会

与南京进行了谈判，据我们所信，这导致外国社群的关键权利和利益一再让步。与1929年一样，在1931年，过早放弃目前享有的此类保障不仅毫无益处，反而会使中国政府和人民陷入困境。

正如一位近期离开天津的著名苏格兰人所指出的那样，我国政府所推行政策的不幸后果之一是，我们被迫“为了防御我们自己政府过于仓促的行动，而强调中国人性格中最糟糕的特征，并且，当我们不愿过于公开谴责时，甚至在本国报刊上大张旗鼓地宣扬中国的耻辱。”我们都知道中国人有优点，但这些优点尚未在司法管理中显现出来。即使是中国的宣传人员，现在也不再仰仗中国法律的优越性。就在几天前的一封信中，我们被邀请成为反对压迫和不公正势力斗争中的“难友”。请注意，“难友”一词。如果我们现在发现难以继续这场斗争，那么当使我们能够继续这场斗争的保障被废除后，困难将会增加多少？我建议，像其他人所做的那样，今晚通过的任何决议都应是一致的。如果有任何具有影响力的本地舆论团体与新成立的这一组织划清界限，那将是致命的。我们必须旨在提出合理的观点，并尽可能争取国内及其他地区中国人的同情，以便促使重新审议治外法权问题。委员会起草了一项决议，对在座的一些人来说，这项决议可能看起来不够强硬，但它确实涵盖了争议的主要要点。英国政府的观点似乎是，局势如此，以至于在明年1月1日之前达成任何新条约总比完全没有条约要好。怎么能严肃地论证必须达成一项条约来取代一项未经我们同意而被中国单方面废除的有效

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI BRITISH RESIDENTS' ASSOCIATION 7

treaty abrogated by the Chinese without our consent ?
I cannot understand that. What possible value can
safeguards existing only on paper have in such a treaty ?
They will be torn to pieces when it suits the Chinese just
as the treaties now in operation are being torn up. Your
Committee are unanimously of the opinion that it would
be preferable to have no treaty at all than to make an
undignified and unwarrantable surrender. For that
reason the Joint Committee has, amongst other things,
cabled Home its emphatic protest against the views ex-
pressed by Sir Harry Fox that the abolition of extra-
territoriality will assist British trade. It now remains
only for me to propose the Resolution, of which you have
copies in your seats, namely :—
“That in view of the present unsettled conditions in
China, the political uncertainty, and the absence
of any stable and authoritative Government,
this meeting of British residents in Shanghai is
unanimously of the opinion that the acceleration
of negotiations regarding the abolition of extra-
territoriality is inadvisable, and that this quest-
ion, and the kindred problems of the future of
Shanghai, Tientsin, Hankow and Shameen should
be reviewed in the light of the obvious inability
or unwillingness of the Nanking Government to
implement its Treaty obligations, or to exercise
effective control over the provincial and military
authorities.”
The resolution was seconded by Mr. A. E. Fenton
and carried unanimously.
page_data.zh:
上海英国侨民协会 7

条约呢？我无法理解这一点。在这样的条约中，仅存在于纸面上的保障措施能有什么可能的价值呢？一旦符合中国人的心意，它们就会被撕得粉碎，就像目前正在执行的条约正被撕毁一样。委员会一致认为，与其做出有失体面且无正当理由的让步，不如根本没有条约。因此，联合委员会除其他事项外，已致电国内，强烈抗议哈里·福克斯爵士（Sir Harry Fox）所表达的观点，即废除治外法权将有助于英国贸易。现在只剩下由我来提出决议，你们座位上有决议副本，即：

“鉴于中国目前的动荡局势、政治上的不确定性，以及缺乏任何稳定且具权威的政府，本次在上海的英国侨民会议一致认为，加速关于废除治外法权的谈判是不明智的；并且，鉴于南京政府显然无力或不愿履行其条约义务，或对地方及军事当局实施有效控制，应在此背景下重新审视治外法权问题，以及上海、天津、汉口和沙面未来的相关问题。”

该决议由 A. E. 芬顿（A. E. Fenton）先生附议，并一致通过。
